snippet.title: Why Everything Is Breaking All at Once | Plain English
snippet.description:
On Friday, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop after communication issues. Then, on Monday, United Airlines announced its own tech outage. That same day, several banks, including JPMorgan and Bank of America, said customers couldn’t withdraw funds because of a software bug. On Tuesday, the NSA announced that its communication systems had been hit by another outage. Then Apple reported difficulties of its own. And before all of this, the FBI issued a Flash warning that cybercriminals and state-aligned hackers were using AI to attack businesses and organizations around the world. Suddenly, the most important question in the news was: Why is everything breaking all at once?

To figure out what’s happening and what we can do about it, Derek welcomes cybersecurity expert Nicole Perlroth and former U.S. deputy chief technology officer Jennifer Pahlka. Is this a coordinated, systemic hack? Is it just engineers rushing to fix vulnerabilities exposed by AI? Is the news media simply more sensitive to outages? Or is something else going on?


If you have questions, observations, or ideas for future episodes, email us at ⁠PlainEnglish@Spotify.com⁠.

snippet.title: El documento que Bank of America llamó falsificación
snippet.description:
El 19 de diciembre de 2003, Bank of America negó que Parmalat tuviera casi 5.000 millones de dólares en activos líquidos. Cinco días después, en Nochebuena, la empresa presentó quiebra con un agujero de 14.000 millones de euros.

Este short sigue el momento en que el fraude saltó: el documento de la filial Bonlat que situaba más de 4.000 millones de euros en las Islas Caimán y que los abogados del banco calificaron de falsificación, la condena de Tanzi a ocho años y un mes, y la absolución de los otros siete acusados del mismo juicio.

snippet.title: How Charlotte Is Becoming America’s Next Skyscraper City
snippet.description:
0:00 The evolution of Charlotte's skyline from a bank-dominated corporate center to a residential-focused urban core.
1:27 NCNB Plaza
3:16 Bank of America Corporate Center
5:48 Duke Energy Center
8:21 Vivian
14:02 Iron District

Charlotte’s skyline is changing—but not in the way you might expect. I trace how a city once shaped by banks and corporate towers is becoming a denser, more residential urban core.

I explore the rise of NCNB Plaza, the Bank of America Corporate Center, and the Duke Energy Center, along with Charlotte’s population growth and the shift of development toward South End. I also look at Vivian, Queensbridge Collective, office conversions, and the changing role of Uptown’s older towers.

Finally, I examine the Iron District and ask what Charlotte’s next phase of growth means for its skyline. The city may not be building much higher, but it is building for a different audience.

snippet.title: Four US Systems Broke in One Week. Was It One Attack?
snippet.description:
In one week in November 2026, an FAA nationwide ground stop, a Microsoft 365 outage, a United Airlines outage and a JPMorgan Chase outage all hit US users, and many people asked whether it was one attack. The FAA, Microsoft, United and Chase each said they saw no sign of a cyberattack. The ground stop was blamed on a technology upgrade that overloaded old equipment (U.S. officials, per AP and NBC) and the Microsoft outage on an issue during a network capacity upgrade (Microsoft, per AP and NBC).

Chase said on X that it had "a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems" and that there was "no evidence this is cyber-related", and said other banks "may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us". Zelle said it does not hold consumer funds and that an issue at banks "may be delaying Zelle payments for some of their customers". Chase said transactions were posting normally by Monday evening.

Mike Chapple of the University of Notre Dame told CBS News that "each one has an explanation that makes sense on its own, but they all point to a common theme: the complexity and fragility of the systems that we depend on every day". NBC reported "no evidence that these incidents are connected to one another".

As of Nov 18, 2026, Chase had not said what set the bug off, which systems it hit, or how many customers it reached. "On-premise hardware" is explained in plain words as machines an organization runs itself; that is our wording, not Chase's. The scene is an illustration, not a map of real systems.

snippet.title: Part 1 - The Fragility Cascade - Three weeks, nine breakdowns, no hacker. Why everything broke?
snippet.description:
The Invisible Tech Fragility Frontline · Part 1 of 4

The Fragility Cascade: When Systems Break Themselves!

Between 27 October and 16 November 2026, a freight railroad, 128 Japanese banks, America's payment rails, a rocket, Microsoft's email, the US air traffic system, a payroll platform, and an airline all failed. So far, no investigator has found a hacker behind any of them. Here is what broke, and why one ordinary change can stop everything.
What broke (as of 18 Nov 2026):
• CSX, 27–28 Oct: a roughly 29-hour outage of almost every system except dispatching and train control; daily volume fell about 46%. CSX blames a cloud problem.
• Shinkin banks, Japan, 6 Nov: one equipment malfunction froze ATMs and counters at 128 banks, mainly in western Japan; "not a cyberattack".
• US banks, 16 Nov: a software bug at JPMorgan Chase; customers at Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo, Capital One, Truist and others reported failures (Downdetector, via CBS). Bank of America says its systems ran normally.
• ULA Vulcan, 15 Nov: mission lost about 10 minutes into flight with 40 Amazon Leo satellites; ULA's first outright failure since 2006. Early data points to low booster performance.
• Microsoft 365, 12 Nov: a bug hidden since July met heavy load and reduced capacity; ~24-hour outage.
• FAA, 13 Nov: newly installed routers flooded the network; 17 of 22 en-route centres hit; every departure halted for over four hours; over 15,000 US flights delayed or cancelled (CNN). Explanations given in four days: old copper lines (Duffy), new security patches (Mullin), routers made 2001–2006 (CBS sources), a router installed by L3Harris (Duffy), "They did not fail" (HPE, owner of router maker Juniper). On 17 Nov the FAA still had no definitive root cause (CNN).
• Amtrak, Workday (13 Nov) and United Airlines (16 Nov, a "widespread system outage"; CBS says ~90 minutes, United told CNN ~30).
• Budapest–Belgrade: passenger launch slipped as Chinese-supplied signalling still needed testing; key ETCS experts resigned (March 2026).
Officials see no coordinated attack; FAA and ULA investigations remain open. Statements are reported with names and dates; no motive is implied.

snippet.title: Banks Say Your AI's Mistakes Are On You. Citi: Even If It's Hacked
snippet.description:
AI vs your money, accounts and data, explained in under a minute.

Citi updated its Online User Agreement this week (TechCrunch, Nov 18, 2026): customers who grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for what those agents do, and if the AI tool leaks their credentials or is hacked, the customer is responsible for what hackers do with the account. A Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch the update is meant to "provide greater clarity" about the risks of sharing banking credentials with third-party AI tools. Citi's terms note that AI agents Citi itself provides can be used without that added liability (per TechCrunch).

Per TechCrunch, JPMorgan and Bank of America announced similar policies last month, PNC changed its terms on Nov 18, and Citizens emailed customers this week warning they're on the hook for anything their AI assistant does (an email seen by TechCrunch).

Separately, Reuters reports that Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said on Nov 18 her office opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies over the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents." She didn't name the other companies or the banks. A criminal investigation does not necessarily mean charges will be brought, and no charges have been announced. OpenAI did not immediately respond to Reuters.

Our take: your login, your risk. If you use an AI money tool, keep it read-only and don't hand it your bank password.

Sources:

snippet.title: Layoffs 2026: 15 of America's top 20 companies cut jobs
snippet.description:
Layoffs 2026 at America's 20 biggest companies (2026 Fortune 500), month by month:
- Jan: Amazon, about 16,000 corporate roles (plus about 14,000 in Oct 2025).
- Feb: Cigna, about 2,000. UnitedHealth confirmed layoffs but gave no number.
- May: Meta, about 8,000 (≈10%), and 6,000 open roles closed. Walmart cut or relocated about 1,000 corporate jobs.
- Jul: Microsoft, about 4,800, Xbox hit hardest; about 1,600 more Xbox roles by mid-2027.
- Aug: Apple, about 200 roles in Siri and Vision Pro.
- WARN notices (60 days' notice for employers with 100+ workers) show smaller cuts at JPMorgan, CVS, Elevance, Bank of America, Google, McKesson and Cardinal Health. Exxon is still carrying out a 2,000-job plan from 2025.
- No 2026 layoffs found at Costco, Nvidia, Cencora or Berkshire Hathaway. Centene used voluntary buyouts.

Cuts with a public number add up to at least 34,000 jobs. That's a floor: many cuts are never numbered. Original animation; 1 figure ≈ 200 jobs.

snippet.title: ACP Presents: Banking on Veteran Talent with Bank of America
snippet.description:
On November 10th, ACP hosted a conversation with Veteran employees at Bank of America focused on transitioning from military service to corporate careers. The webinar explored the valuable skills Veterans bring to the workplace and how military experience can translate into meaningful career opportunities.

The session featured Hector Santiago-Perez, Assistant Vice President, Process Design and Project Management, Army Veteran and Global Financial Crimes Investigative Specialist; Al Williams, Assistant Vice President, Business Support Management and Army Veteran; and Heidi Card, Senior Vice President, GBP Release and Change Management and Navy Veteran. Through their personal stories and career experiences, they shared insights on navigating the transition to the civilian workforce, building rewarding careers after military service, and applying military-developed leadership, problem-solving, adaptability, and teamwork skills in the workplace.

Attendees gained practical advice on navigating career transitions, exploring professional opportunities beyond military service, and leveraging their military experience to succeed in the corporate workforce.

snippet.title: Chase Bank OUTAGE Leaves Payments STUCK For Hours As Bank Of America Fargo Customers Report Problems
snippet.description:
On Monday, November 16, 2026, thousands of customers reported trouble with banking at JPMorgan Chase, and with payments at Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank and others. Chase said the cause was "a software bug in on-premise hardware systems" and that it was not cyber-related. Around 6:30 p.m. Eastern it said transactions were posting normally again.

This video goes through what happened in order, using the banks' own statements: when the reports began, what customers said they could not do, what Chase said and how its wording changed, what Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Capital One, Truist, PNC and Zelle each said, why a problem at one bank can delay a payment at another, what is still unanswered, and what to do if one of your payments was delayed.

In this video:
0:00 "The whole system is down"
0:47 Monday morning
2:05 What Chase said
2:47 The other banks
4:22 Back to normal
4:47 The week
5:50 What is not known
6:16 If your payment got stuck

Information as of Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Only Chase confirmed a problem with its own systems. Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Capital One, Truist and PNC said their systems were operating normally or were not directly affected; Wells Fargo declined to comment to Reuters. Zelle said it was not down. Chase said customers kept access to their accounts and funds; some customers reported that they could not make withdrawals or deposits. Both are reported here with their source.

Downdetector figures are user-submitted reports at a point in time, not a count of affected customers. The account that the problem came from a software release rolled out earlier on Monday is Fox Business's, citing an FBI official it did not name; Chase has not described it that way. The start time is given differently by different sources (between about 9 a.m. and noon Eastern). Bank share prices fell about 2% on a day when the wider market also fell; Barron's reported that no direct connection had been established. Chase has not said how many customers or transactions were affected, which systems failed, or whether every delayed payment has posted, and we found no Chase statement about late fees or overdrafts. News organizations reported no evidence linking the bank outage to the Microsoft outage or the FAA ground stop the week before. The advice in the last chapter is from consumer and security experts quoted by CBS News, not from the banks. This is not financial advice. News clips are short excerpts shown with their source and date on screen.

SOURCES
- JPMorgan Chase statements of Nov. 16, 2026 (as published by the Associated Press, Reuters, NBC News, CNBC and LiveNOW from Fox)
- Zelle / Early Warning Services statement, Nov. 16, 2026 (NBC News and others)
- Statements of Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Capital One, Truist and PNC, Nov. 16-17, 2026 (Fox Business, Newsweek, NBC News, CBS News, Politico)
- Associated Press, Reuters, NBC News, CBS News, ABC News, CNN, Fox Business, Banking Dive, Barron's, Nov. 16-17, 2026
- Chase and Zelle company figures: Chase news release of Nov. 10, 2026; Zelle release of Feb. 11, 2026
- Remarks by Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin (CNBC) and President Trump, Nov. 17, 2026, as reported by CNN and NBC News
- Broadcast clips: ABC World News Tonight, NBC Nightly News, NBC Early Today, CBS Evening News, CNN, Fox News, KTVU and NBC Bay Area, via the Internet Archive TV News Archive

In this video:
0:00 "The whole system is down"
0:47 Monday morning
2:05 What Chase said
2:47 The other banks
4:22 Back to normal
4:47 The week
5:50 What is not known
6:16 If your payment got stuck

Information as of Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Only Chase confirmed a problem with its own systems. Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Capital One, Truist and PNC said their systems were operating normally or were not directly affected; Wells Fargo declined to comment to Reuters. Zelle said it was not down. Chase said customers kept access to their accounts and funds; some customers reported that they could not make withdrawals or deposits. Both are reported here with their source.

Downdetector figures are user-submitted reports at a point in time, not a count of affected customers. The account that the problem came from a software release rolled out earlier on Monday is Fox Business's, citing an FBI official it did not name; Chase has not described it that way. The start time is given differently by different sources (between about 9 a.m. and noon Eastern). Bank share prices fell about 2% on a day when the wider market also fell; Barron's reported that no direct connection had been established. Chase has not said how many customers or transactions were affected, which systems failed, or whether every delayed payment has posted, and we found no Chase statement about late fees or overdrafts. News organizations reported no evidence linking the bank outage to the Microsoft outage or the FAA ground stop the week before. The advice in the last chapter is from consumer and security experts quoted by CBS News, not from the banks. This is not financial advice. snippet.title: Nvidia 董事會無意讓黃仁勳復任｜Druckenmiller 進入保本模式 ｜市場消息焦點 ｜2026年 11月 18日
snippet.description:
內容簡介
黃仁勳離任後，臨時行政總裁 Colette Kress 首次公布 Nvidia 業績：第三財季營收 1,158 億美元，第四財季營收指引 1,300 億美元，2028 財年營收增長指引調高至約 75%，均高於市場預期；第四財季毛利率指引則由第三財季的 74.8% 降至 71% 至 72%。股價盤後一度急升 5.4%，到亞洲時段升幅收窄至約 1.4%。

董事會主席 Harvey Jones 在業績電話會議上表明，無意讓黃仁勳復任。業績附帶的 CFO 書面評論亦列明，Nvidia 與 Neocloud 協議相關的 320 億美元承諾，須對方取得融資、產能投入運作並經 Nvidia 驗收才生效。本片同時整理時事評論員的預測、Sam Altman 的回應、大股東聯名致函董事會、Polymarket 年底前回歸機率、Situational Awareness 持倉市值減少 92%、美銀基金經理調查，以及 Druckenmiller 進入保本模式的最新看法。
